title: 👑 Elite Challenge: Relative Clauses & Comparatives Under Pressure

questions.prompt: Join the two sentences: "I saw the boys. The boys were throwing rubbish into the river."

options.text: I saw the boys which were throwing rubbish into the river.
I saw the boys who they were throwing rubbish into the river.
I saw the boys that they were throwing rubbish into the river.
I saw the boys who were throwing rubbish into the river.

questions.explanation: "The boys" are persons and the subject of "were throwing", so "who" replaces them and no pronoun follows: the boys who were throwing rubbish. "Which" cannot refer to people, and the tempting "who they" / "that they" give the verb a second subject.

questions.prompt: One word fits BOTH blanks: "People ___ drop litter and cars ___ release fumes pollute our town."

options.text: who
which
that
what

questions.explanation: The first blank follows a person (people), the second a thing (cars); only "that" refers to both. "Who" fits only the first blank, "which" only the second, and "what" is not a relative pronoun.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Ali's joke is ___ than Sami's, but Nour's joke is ___ of all." (silly)

options.text: sillier / the silliest
more silly / the most silly
sillyer / the sillyest
sillier / the sillier

questions.explanation: "Silly" ends with a consonant + y, so the y becomes i: sillier (two jokes) and the silliest (the top of all). "Sillyer" keeps the y, "more / the most" are for long adjectives, and "the sillier" uses a comparative where "of all" needs a superlative.

questions.prompt: Sami's bag weighs 4 kg. Hedi's bag weighs 4 kg, too. Which sentence is TRUE?

options.text: Sami's bag is heavier than Hedi's.
Sami's bag is as heavy as Hedi's.
Hedi's bag is heavier than Sami's.
Sami's bag is as heavier as Hedi's.

questions.explanation: 4 kg = 4 kg, so the bags are equal: as + plain adjective + as, as heavy as. Both "heavier than" sentences are false, because neither bag is heavier, and "as heavier as" puts a comparative inside the structure.

questions.prompt: Tunis, Sfax and Sousse are three big cities. Complete: "Of the three, Tunis is ___."

options.text: bigger
the biggest
the bigger
the most big

questions.explanation: Tunis is compared with a group of three, so we need the superlative: "big" ends with one vowel + one consonant, so the g doubles: the biggest. "Bigger" and "the bigger" are comparatives, and "the most" is only for long adjectives.

questions.prompt: A student writes: "My sister is as more intelligent as me." Choose the correct version.

options.text: My sister is as intelligent as me.
My sister is more intelligent as me.
My sister is as intelligenter as me.
My sister is the most intelligent as me.

questions.explanation: Equality keeps the plain adjective between the two "as", even a long one: as intelligent as. "More … as" mixes the comparative with the equality, "intelligenter" adds -er to a long adjective, and a superlative cannot be followed by "as me".
